VPC with private subnets, NACLs, Security Groups, PrivateLink, KMS, and GuardDuty
Default VPC settings with internet gateway and basic encryption
questions.explanation: Zero-trust architecture requires: VPC with private subnets for network isolation, NACLs and Security Groups for microsegmentation, PrivateLink for secure service communication, KMS for end-to-end encryption, and GuardDuty for continuous threat monitoring.

questions.question: A media streaming company experiences highly variable traffic with 10x spikes during live events. They need a cost-optimized architecture that automatically scales and minimizes costs during low-traffic periods. Which combination provides the MOST cost-effective solution?
options: Auto Scaling Groups with mixed instance types, Spot Instances, and CloudFront
questions.explanation: Auto Scaling Groups with mixed instance types provide flexibility, Spot Instances offer up to 90% savings for fault-tolerant workloads during spikes, and CloudFront reduces origin load and costs through global caching, optimizing costs across traffic variations.
validation_sources: AWS cost optimization for variable workloads

questions.question: A pharmaceutical company needs to run complex drug discovery simulations requiring thousands of CPU cores for short periods, with strict data security and compliance requirements. Which AWS approach BEST meets these requirements while optimizing costs?
options: Single large EC2 instance running continuously
AWS Batch with Spot Instances in a private VPC with encryption
questions.explanation: AWS Batch automatically manages compute resources for batch workloads, Spot Instances provide up to 90% cost savings for fault-tolerant simulations, private VPC ensures security isolation, and encryption meets pharmaceutical compliance requirements.

questions.question: A multinational corporation with 50+ AWS accounts needs centralized cost management, governance, and compliance monitoring across all accounts. Which AWS services combination provides comprehensive multi-account management?
options: Individual account management with manual reporting
AWS Organizations with Control Tower, consolidated billing, and Security Hub
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations enables multi-account management, Control Tower provides governance and compliance guardrails, consolidated billing offers volume discounts and centralized cost management, and Security Hub provides centralized security posture across all accounts.

questions.question: A retail company needs to implement a real-time recommendation engine that processes customer behavior data, updates ML models continuously, and serves recommendations with sub-100ms latency globally. Which architecture BEST supports these requirements?
options: Batch processing with daily model updates
Manual data processing with weekly updates
Kinesis Data Streams, Lambda, DynamoDB Global Tables, and CloudFront
questions.explanation: Kinesis Data Streams processes real-time customer behavior, Lambda enables serverless model updates, DynamoDB Global Tables provide sub-100ms global access to recommendations, and CloudFront ensures global low-latency delivery.

questions.question: A government agency needs to migrate classified data to AWS while maintaining air-gapped security, FIPS 140-2 Level 3 compliance, and ensuring data never leaves government-controlled infrastructure. Which AWS solution BEST meets these stringent requirements?
options: AWS GovCloud with CloudHSM FIPS 140-2 Level 3 and dedicated tenancy
questions.explanation: AWS GovCloud provides FedRAMP High authorized environment for classified data, CloudHSM FIPS 140-2 Level 3 provides hardware-based key management meeting the highest security standards, and dedicated tenancy ensures physical isolation.

questions.question: A startup is building a serverless application that needs to handle unpredictable traffic from 10 to 100,000 concurrent users, process images, store metadata, and send notifications. Which architecture provides the MOST scalable and cost-effective solution?
options: API Gateway, Lambda, S3, DynamoDB, and SNS
Single large server with manual scaling
questions.explanation: This serverless architecture automatically scales: API Gateway handles traffic spikes, Lambda processes requests without server management, S3 stores images with unlimited capacity, DynamoDB scales automatically, and SNS handles notifications, all with pay-per-use pricing.

questions.question: A large enterprise has complex billing requirements with 200+ accounts, multiple business units, and needs detailed chargeback allocation with cost optimization recommendations. Which comprehensive cost management strategy provides the BEST results?
options: AWS Organizations, Cost Categories, Savings Plans, and automated RI management
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations enables consolidated billing across 200+ accounts, Cost Categories provide automated chargeback allocation to business units, Savings Plans offer flexible discounts, and automated RI management optimizes Reserved Instance utilization and exchanges.

questions.question: A research institution needs to store 500TB of genomic sequencing data with varying access patterns — some datasets are accessed daily, others monthly, and archival data is rarely accessed. They want to minimize storage costs automatically. Which S3 storage approach is MOST cost-effective?
options: S3 Standard for all data to ensure consistent performance
S3 Glacier for all data to minimize costs
S3 Standard with manual lifecycle policies to Glacier after 90 days
S3 Intelligent-Tiering to automatically move data between access tiers based on usage patterns
questions.explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between access tiers (Frequent, Infrequent, Archive) based on actual access patterns, optimizing costs without manual intervention or retrieval fees. For 500TB with varying access patterns, this eliminates the need to predict access frequency. S3 Standard is expensive for rarely accessed data. S3 Glacier has retrieval delays unsuitable for daily-accessed data. Manual lifecycle policies require predicting access patterns upfront.

questions.question: A financial institution needs to implement a comprehensive security monitoring solution that detects threats, ensures compliance with multiple frameworks (SOC 2, PCI DSS), and provides automated incident response. Which AWS services combination provides the MOST comprehensive security solution?
options: Security Hub, GuardDuty, Config, CloudTrail, and Lambda for automation
questions.explanation: Security Hub centralizes security findings and compliance status, GuardDuty detects threats using ML, Config monitors compliance with SOC 2 and PCI DSS rules, CloudTrail provides audit trails, and Lambda enables automated incident response workflows.

questions.question: A global e-commerce company needs to implement a data lake architecture that ingests data from multiple sources, processes it in real-time and batch modes, and provides analytics capabilities while optimizing costs. Which architecture BEST meets these requirements?
options: S3 data lake with Kinesis, Glue, EMR, Athena, and lifecycle policies
Basic file storage with manual analysis
questions.explanation: S3 provides scalable data lake foundation, Kinesis handles real-time ingestion, Glue provides serverless ETL, EMR handles big data processing, Athena enables serverless analytics, and lifecycle policies optimize storage costs across different access patterns.

questions.question: A manufacturing company wants to implement predictive maintenance using IoT sensors, machine learning, and real-time alerts. They need to process sensor data, detect anomalies, and trigger maintenance workflows. Which AWS architecture BEST supports this IoT and ML use case?
options: IoT Core, Kinesis Analytics, SageMaker, Lambda, and SNS
questions.explanation: IoT Core manages sensor connectivity, Kinesis Analytics processes streaming sensor data in real-time, SageMaker provides ML models for anomaly detection, Lambda triggers maintenance workflows, and SNS sends real-time alerts to maintenance teams.

questions.question: A media company has significant data transfer costs representing 40% of their AWS bill due to global content distribution. They need to optimize these costs while maintaining performance and implementing geographic content restrictions. Which strategy provides the GREATEST cost reduction?
options: Reduce content quality to minimize transfer
CloudFront with Lambda@Edge, S3 Intelligent-Tiering, and regional optimization
questions.explanation: CloudFront significantly reduces data transfer costs through edge caching, as content served from edge locations is charged at a lower rate than standard origin data transfer. Lambda@Edge enables geographic restrictions without additional infrastructure, S3 Intelligent-Tiering optimizes storage costs, and regional optimization minimizes cross-region transfer charges.

questions.question: A development team wants to improve their ability to run and monitor systems to deliver business value and continuously improve processes. Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar directly addresses this goal?
questions.explanation: The Operational Excellence pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework focuses on running and monitoring systems to deliver business value and continually improving supporting processes and procedures. It includes the ability to support development, run workloads effectively, gain insight into operations, and continuously improve. Reliability focuses on workload recovery; Performance Efficiency on using computing resources efficiently; Security on protecting systems and data.
validation_sources: AWS Well-Architected Framework - Operational Excellence Pillar

questions.question: A company needs to ensure their e-commerce platform can automatically recover from infrastructure failures and dynamically acquire computing resources to meet demand. Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar guides these capabilities?
questions.explanation: The Reliability pillar focuses on ensuring a workload performs its intended function correctly and consistently when expected. It includes the ability to automatically recover from infrastructure or service disruptions, dynamically acquire computing resources to meet demand, and mitigate disruptions. Operational Excellence focuses on running and monitoring systems; Performance Efficiency on using resources efficiently; Cost Optimization on avoiding unnecessary costs.

questions.question: An organization wants to minimize the environmental impact of their cloud workloads by reducing energy consumption and improving resource utilization. Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar should guide their efforts?
questions.explanation: The Sustainability pillar focuses on minimizing the environmental impacts of running cloud workloads. It covers understanding the impact of workloads, maximizing resource utilization, minimizing required infrastructure, and reducing downstream environmental impacts. Although Cost Optimization also reduces resource usage, its goal is financial savings — not environmental impact. Sustainability is the pillar specifically dedicated to environmental responsibility.

questions.question: A company wants to migrate their on-premises application to AWS as quickly as possible with minimal changes to take advantage of cloud infrastructure. They have no budget for code refactoring. Which migration strategy should they use?
questions.explanation: Rehost (lift and shift) involves moving applications to the cloud with no changes to the application code or architecture. It is the fastest migration strategy and requires minimal effort. Replatform involves making a few cloud optimizations without changing core architecture. Refactor involves redesigning the application to fully leverage cloud-native features, which requires significant development effort. Repurchase involves moving to a different product entirely, such as a SaaS solution.

questions.question: A company's HR department needs to understand how cloud adoption will affect employee roles, organizational structure, and training requirements. Which AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) perspective addresses these concerns?
questions.explanation: The AWS CAF People perspective focuses on culture, organizational structure, leadership, and workforce skills needed for cloud adoption. It helps organizations identify capability gaps and how roles will evolve with cloud adoption. The Business perspective aligns IT with business needs; the Governance perspective focuses on portfolio management and risk; the Platform perspective covers architecture and infrastructure. HR concerns about roles, training, and organizational impact fall squarely in the People perspective.

questions.question: A company currently spends $500,000 per year on data center hardware, cooling, and facilities staff. They are evaluating AWS migration. Which cloud economic benefit would MOST directly reduce these specific costs?
options: Eliminating capital expenditure on data center infrastructure
Paying lower per-unit prices due to AWS economies of scale
Using Reserved Instances for predictable workloads
Enabling global deployment for new revenue opportunities
questions.explanation: Moving to AWS eliminates the need to invest in and maintain physical data center infrastructure — hardware, cooling systems, and facilities staff. This directly converts fixed capital expenditures (CapEx) into variable operating expenses (OpEx). Economies of scale refers to AWS passing cost savings to customers through lower pricing. Reserved Instances reduce compute costs but don't address facilities costs. Global deployment creates business opportunities but doesn't reduce existing data center costs.
validation_sources: AWS Cloud Economics - Total Cost of Ownership
AWS Well-Architected Framework Cost Optimization pillar

questions.question: A developer wants to experiment with Amazon EC2 and Amazon S3 for the first time without incurring charges. Which AWS Free Tier offering provides 750 hours of EC2 t2.micro usage per month for 12 months?
questions.explanation: The AWS 12-month free tier provides new AWS customers with free usage of certain services for 12 months from account creation. This includes 750 hours/month of EC2 t2.micro or t3.micro instances and 5 GB of S3 standard storage. The Always Free tier covers services like AWS Lambda (1M requests/month) and DynamoDB (25 GB storage) with no time limit. Free trials are short-term offers for specific services. There is no 'AWS Educate tier' as a standard Free Tier category.

questions.question: A company has 50 developers who all need the same read-only access to Amazon S3. What is the MOST efficient IAM approach to manage their permissions?
options: Create an IAM group with the S3 read-only policy and add all developers as members
Create an IAM role with the S3 read-only policy and assign it to each developer
Attach the S3 read-only policy directly to each developer's IAM user
Create one shared IAM user with S3 read-only access for all developers
questions.explanation: IAM groups allow you to attach policies to multiple users at once. By creating a group with the S3 read-only policy and adding all 50 developers as members, permissions are centrally managed — if the policy needs updating, you change it once on the group. Assigning a role to each developer is incorrect because roles are assumed temporarily, not assigned to users. Attaching policies directly to each user requires 50 separate policy attachments and 50 updates if permissions change. Sharing one IAM user violates the security best practice of individual accountability.

questions.question: A company is running an application on an Amazon EC2 instance that needs to read objects from an S3 bucket. What is the AWS BEST PRACTICE for granting this access?
options: Assign an IAM role with S3 read permissions to the EC2 instance
Create an IAM user, generate access keys, and store them in the application code
Create an IAM user, generate access keys, and store them as environment variables on the EC2 instance
Enable public access on the S3 bucket so the EC2 instance can read without credentials
questions.explanation: The best practice is to use IAM roles for applications running on EC2. An IAM role provides temporary security credentials automatically rotated by AWS — no long-term credentials need to be stored or managed. Storing access keys in application code is a critical security risk because keys could be exposed if the code is shared. Storing keys as environment variables is safer than code but still uses long-term credentials that require manual rotation. Making an S3 bucket public exposes it to everyone on the internet.
validation_sources: AWS IAM Best Practices - Use roles for applications

questions.question: A healthcare company is preparing for a HIPAA audit and needs to provide auditors with AWS compliance reports and AWS agreements such as the Business Associate Addendum (BAA). Where can they download these documents?
questions.explanation: AWS Artifact is a self-service portal for accessing AWS compliance documentation and AWS agreements. It provides on-demand access to AWS security and compliance reports such as SOC reports, PCI DSS, ISO certifications, and the ability to review and accept AWS agreements like the Business Associate Addendum (BAA) required for HIPAA workloads. AWS Security Hub aggregates security findings but does not provide compliance documents. AWS Config tracks resource configuration changes. AWS Trusted Advisor provides best practice recommendations.

questions.question: A company is running a serverless application using AWS Lambda. According to the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, which of the following is the CUSTOMER's responsibility?
options: Writing secure application code and managing IAM permissions for Lambda functions
Patching and maintaining the underlying server infrastructure that runs Lambda
Managing the operating system on which Lambda functions execute
Ensuring physical security of the data centers where Lambda runs
questions.explanation: In the Shared Responsibility Model, AWS manages the infrastructure 'of' the cloud (hardware, networking, hypervisor, and for Lambda — the underlying servers, OS, and runtime environment). Customers are responsible for security 'in' the cloud — this includes writing secure application code, managing IAM permissions and execution roles, protecting environment variables/secrets, and controlling what data is processed. With serverless services like Lambda, the customer's infrastructure responsibility is reduced but code-level and access security remain entirely the customer's responsibility.

questions.question: A financial services company needs to continuously collect evidence of their AWS resource configurations and user activities to simplify the process of preparing for regulatory audits. Which AWS service automates evidence collection for compliance audits?
questions.explanation: AWS Audit Manager continuously collects evidence from AWS services and maps it to compliance framework controls (such as PCI DSS, HIPAA, SOC 2, and FedRAMP) to help simplify audit preparation. It automates evidence gathering from AWS CloudTrail, AWS Config, Security Hub, and other sources. AWS Config tracks configuration changes but doesn't map them to compliance frameworks or generate audit-ready reports. AWS CloudTrail records API activity but requires manual analysis for audits. AWS Security Hub aggregates security findings but is not specifically designed for audit evidence collection.

questions.question: A company with 20 AWS accounts in an AWS Organization needs to enforce a standard set of AWS WAF rules across all accounts and automatically apply them to new accounts as they are created. Which AWS service enables this centralized security management?
questions.explanation: AWS Firewall Manager is a security management service that allows you to centrally configure and manage firewall rules — including AWS WAF rules, AWS Shield Advanced protections, and VPC security groups — across all accounts in an AWS Organization. It automatically applies policies to new accounts and resources as they are created. AWS WAF is the underlying service that blocks web traffic, but it must be configured account by account without Firewall Manager. AWS Shield provides DDoS protection. Amazon GuardDuty is a threat detection service, not a centralized firewall management tool.

questions.question: A company has just created a new AWS account. Which task requires the use of the AWS account root user and CANNOT be performed by an IAM administrator user?
options: Enabling multi-factor authentication on IAM users
questions.explanation: Closing an AWS account is one of the tasks that requires the root user — it cannot be delegated to IAM users or roles. Other root-user-only tasks include changing the account's email address, changing the AWS support plan, enabling IAM access to billing, restoring IAM user permissions, and registering as a seller in AWS Marketplace. Creating IAM users and groups, attaching IAM policies, and enabling MFA on IAM users are all tasks that can be performed by an IAM user with the appropriate administrative permissions.
validation_sources: AWS IAM documentation - Tasks that require root user credentials

questions.question: A security team wants to ensure that all IAM users in their AWS account use strong passwords and that their passwords expire after 90 days. Which AWS feature should they configure?
questions.explanation: IAM account password policy allows administrators to define password requirements for all IAM users in the account, including minimum length, required character types, password expiration period (e.g., 90 days), password reuse prevention, and whether users can change their own passwords. This policy applies to all IAM users. AWS Secrets Manager rotates application secrets and API keys, not IAM user passwords. AWS Config can check compliance but does not enforce password policies directly. AWS Shield is a DDoS protection service, not related to password management.
